posts.cooked: With ten minions in the trash, Forced Deployment is an instant win for Voss if not killed before his turn, isn't it?

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
Nope.

Do the start of turn effects in the order they entered play.

Voss checks for win conditions, then Forced Deployment brings back minions from the trash.

You have until the next start of villain turn to reduce the number of minions below 10.

 

If you're talking about destroying Forced Deployment during a hero turn, then all the heroes that come after the destroy effect can attack the minions to take them below the magical number 10, if you can't do any damage then yes, you have destroyed Forced Deployment in order to let Voss win!

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: I was referring to if you have a lot of Minions in the trash and Forced Deployment comes out, it's in your interest to nuke it ASAP so that you hav the rest of the round to subsequently nuke as many Minions as possible. Otherwise you are guaranteed for all of them to attack you at the end of Voss's turn. If you can bring them out on the first hero's turn and have the other heroes (and/or that hero as well) take out as many as you can, you'll get less of a beating (or none at all, obviously, if you can take them all out).

posts.name: Hardboiledgregg
posts.cooked:
Speaking as a relative novice and in my experience with my friends, it's best to try and keep things as simple as possible. They didn't get hooked like I did, but did enjoy the odd game depending on what hero they played and the only frustrations were when too many variables came into play (different strokes for different folks there though) usually thanks to the environment and all sorts of minions. While I doubt you'd have any trouble running the game, it would probably help not to overwhelm newer players when it comes to considering the trickier effects (redirects and other possible odd chains, for example).

When we played last, I also demoed Iron Legacy, explaining that he was pretty evil (we'd won every game before that) and they got fed up with figuring out all the different plays ("So, with this next ongoing we deal the damage to ourselves? OK, let's see what the modifiers are there…", "If I play this card, do I still take the damage first?", "I guess I just don't do anything this turn…", "Player with the highest HP takes this, then the player with the lowest…ugh" ) I know it's pretty basic for experienced players, but it kills the flow for newer ones.

For my first ever game, I really enjoyed Tempest, purely because you did have all those options at your disposal. I think most newer players want to get involved more in dealing damage, but perhaps not have it too simplified like with Ra. Tempest seems to cover everything here. Or possibly even Wraith once she gets going. And, of course, everyone loves Batman.

One (smart) friend who played a good Visionary in his second game, didn't enjoy it that much, but really enjoyed his third game as Absolute Zero because once he was set up, he could easily wipe a load of Voss' minions in a single turn (and I spent a good deal of the game tanking as Legacy, which was cool) but I'm not sure he'd suit most people. It could be useful to have him in a game to show off the more high-level play without getting too complex, however. Same goes for Visionary, really.

All I know is that nearly all my friends found Legacy, Ra, Mr. Fixer and Expatriette too samey; Visionary too non-aggressive(!); and Unity too slow to get going. Others I haven't mentioned never really got to the table because my friends always wanted to use the randomizer (really not a good idea for beginners, I don't think, and definitely didn't help their enthusiasm) or I didn't have some of the expansions earlier on.

Now, obviously, my friends aren't necessarily the typical bunch, but they seem to match what I would consider a blind assessment.

So, that said, I would probably go with something like you as Legacy, them as Tempest or Wraith (but both in the game), and Visionary, in order to get a decent mix. Possibly add AZ or substitute him for Wraith - not sure on that one.

Villain-wise, like I said, I think getting bogged down with minion or other effects could kill things until they're more experienced and appreciate the nuances of the game; though Dawn might be manageable and has interesting flip mechanics (minion-pairing shenanigans could be a problem though?). Omnitron or Baron Blade are safe starters because they still have that variety without being too complex.

As for the environment, I'm not too sure as I don't actually have experience with all of them yet, nor do I have Infernal Relics, to which I've seen folks make reference. As far as I can recall, Insula Primalis and Ruins of Atlantis keep you on your toes. Time Cataclysm is fun and might help liven things up.

Hope some of that massive ramble helps.

I've been in that kind of situation, where the new player is overwhelmed by choices.  I'm usually afraid talking about what they are "supposed to be doing" will make them think there are right and wrong answers as far as card plays, and thereby make them more nervous.  Typically I'll just tell them to take as long as they need to read all their cards and reread the back of the rulebook (Play a card, use a power, draw a card to end your turn).  That explanation can vary a little when they need to know the difference between ongoings, equipment, and one-off cards, though.

I find most people will figure out the general idea behind any one character about the time they've seen and read 10 of their cards (usually the opening hand and 5/7 turns).  Yeah, they won't get the minute details, but learning those is the draw to playing more.  If they don't want to learn those details, then this game might just not be for them.

posts.name: danmarshall14
posts.cooked:
Hey Envisioner,

 

I've had the most success giving newer players Tempest, Tachyon, and Visionary (depending on their personalities/preferences).  Tempest always feels like he's being relevant, with several powers and ongoings that hit several enemies.  Have someone on your team play Legacy and give him a damage buff and your friend is sure to enjoy swatting down minions like flies.  Tachyon is in a similar vain; she always feels like she's doing something.  She can typically play a lot of cards in a turn which makes your turns feel more fun, and once you get ahold of her "count your burst cards" attacks, it can be a blast racking up a big hit.

 

Visionary is a little different; I'd let her use her if she wants something more complicated than Tempest/Tachyon, yet is okay having control rather than dealing damage (most of my friends hate Visionary because they don't find deck manipulation fun; they'd rather be bursting down minions with Ra).  But on the rare instance you get someone on your team who likes that sort of gameplay, Visionary is perfect for them.

 

When choosing an environment, I say Silver Gulch.  It's thematic and a little cheeky, yet is pretty balanced in terms of aiding/hurting the players.

 

For bosses, I'd say someone who is easier, yet still provides some fun twists.  Voss and his Forced Deployment can cause a complete "Oh ****!" moment for everyone, creating a fun yet tense moment as you all pool your heads together to figure out how to deal with the impending army.  Baron Blade has a little bit of everything; he creates a dramatic early game with his moon beam (and if your friend plays Visionary, she'll have fun using her deck manipulation to put the Villain trash on the bottom of the deck) and has enough threatening cards to create a good, medium difficulty.

 

Others that can be fun are Gloomweaver (easy, but thematically awesome with his zombies and cultists and relics) and Apostate, though don't let her use Tempest against him since he has a few ways to get -1 damage, which can make it boring.
